perProductFindings.note: Full per-vendor detail (pricing model, migration constraints, hosting, commercial support, developer/agency fit, sources checked, confidence, unknown fields) is in lib/cms-decision-matrix/data.ts and was researched live tonight via a parallel 8-agent workflow. Summarized here.

wordpress.note: The only one of 8 with a documented path in BOTH directions -- exports an open WXR/XML format.

umbraco.note: No official import-from-other-CMS tooling found; export-out exists only Umbraco-to-Umbraco (Deploy/Packages), not to a competitor.

craft-cms.note: Official first-party WordPress importer exists; no documented export-out path to any competitor.

drupal.note: Migrate API is explicitly one-directional (into Drupal only).

joomla.note: Official WordPress-to-Joomla importer (built via Google Summer of Code 2025) exists; no export-out tooling found.

webflow.note: Vendor's own FAQ states flatly: no import of an existing site/code is possible. Export-out exists for static content only; dynamic content/forms break on export and cannot be reimported anywhere, including back into Webflow.

contentful.note: Own CLI export/import moves content between Contentful spaces in Contentful's proprietary schema only -- not a path to any other CMS.

storyblok.note: Extensive official migration-IN guides exist for named competitors (Contentful, Drupal); no official export-OUT path documented.

theOneReusableFramework: Migration direction (import-in vs. export-out, both vendor-documented or not) is the single strongest, most defensible, most citable cross-vendor finding: 5 of 8 document import-only, 2 of 8 (Umbraco, Webflow) document export-only with no documented import path, 1 of 8 (WordPress) documents both, and 0 of 8 document neither. This became the spine of the new /research/cms-buying-decision-2026 asset rather than a generic pricing comparison, which the existing SaaS Pricing Pressure Index already covers at a sitewide level.
